answer: Each agent’s reputation can be tied to a vault-backed stake that is slashed when its signed actions are proven fraudulent. A grove of independent validators checks those actions against public evidence before triggering a penalty, so one operator cannot cheaply manufacture trusted identities. Sybils may still join, but each must lock real capital; spreading control across many accounts multiplies the funds at risk, while withdrawing stake sacrifices accumulated reputation. Even shale-hard rules cannot prevent collusion, but they make it costly.
